content.content:
N0="$W/jshadow-classes:$W/nat0-classes"; N1n="$W/jshadow-classes:$W/nat1-classes"
N1="$W/jshadow-classes:$W/tri-classes:$W/nat1-classes"; PO="$W/tri-ponly-classes:$W/ponly-classes"
dP="-Dprobe.zero.dropP=true"; eN="-Dprobe.zero.eligibleNarrow=true"; H="-Dprobe.triage.dropPHier=true"
O="-Dprobe.triage.dropPOver=true"; M="-Dfortress.analyzer.overload.cache=false"; DG="-Dprobe.triage.diag=true"
wf () { local out=$1 pre=$2 lib=$3; shift 3                # one whole compilation unit, private cache
  local c=$W/c-$out; rm -rf $c; mkdir -p $c; printf '\0\0\0\0' > $c/global.map
  { echo "########## WorldFlip $lib  ${*:-}"; local s=$(date +%s)
    timeout 3000 java -Xmx4g -Xss64m -XX:-OmitStackTraceInFastThrow "$@" -Dfortress.caches=$c \
      -cp "$pre:$W/pshadow-classes:$CP:$W" WorldFlip $W/lib/$lib/FortressLibrary.fss
    echo "exit=$?"; echo "ELAPSED $(( $(date +%s) - s )) s"; } > $W/$out.out 2>&1
  echo "$out $(grep -oE 'has [0-9]+ errors?' $W/$out.out | tail -1)"; }
# 1. the two copies of the brief, in zero's own classes
wf r01-ZALL3-dP-eN             "$N0"  ZALL3 $dP $eN          # everything applied: 173
wf r06-ZALL3-dP-eN-again       "$N0"  ZALL3 $dP $eN
wf r02-ZL-dP                   "$N0"  ZL    $dP              # batch 3 as written, zero's (broad) switch
# 2. the placements, and the pair memo that makes the fill count depend on the build
wf r26-ZALL3-dP-eN-nat1-notri  "$N1n" ZALL3 $dP $eN
wf r03-ZALL3-dP-eN-nat1        "$N1"  ZALL3 $dP $eN
wf r16-ZALL3-dP-eN-nat1-again  "$N1"  ZALL3 $dP $eN
wf r05-ZALL3-HO-eN             "$N1"  ZALL3 $H $O $eN
wf r04-ZALL3-H-eN              "$N1"  ZALL3 $H $eN
wf r09-ZL-H                    "$N1"  ZL    $H
wf r07-ZALL3-dP-eN-diag        "$N1"  ZALL3 $dP $eN $DG
wf r15-ZALL3-HO-eN-diag        "$N1"  ZALL3 $H $O $eN $DG
wf r20-ZALL3-dP-eN-nat0-nomemo "$N0"  ZALL3 $dP $eN $M
wf r21-ZALL3-dP-eN-nat1-nomemo "$N1"  ZALL3 $dP $eN $M
wf r25-ZALL3-HO-eN-nomemo      "$N1"  ZALL3 $H $O $eN $M
wf r24-ZALL3-H-eN-nomemo       "$N1"  ZALL3 $H $eN $M
# 3. the fixes, cumulative, memo off
for v in T1 T2 T3; do wf r3$v-dP-eN-nomemo "$N0" $v $dP $eN $M; done
# 4. batch 3 on the current tree
wf r13-cur-L0-H        "$PO" L0 $H                          # rung P alone
wf r27-cur-ZL-noP      "$PO" ZL                             # rung L alone
wf r11-cur-ZL-H        "$PO" ZL $H                          # the batch
wf r19-cur-ZL-H-again  "$PO" ZL $H
wf r22-cur-ZL-H-nomemo "$PO" ZL $H $M
wf r12-cur-ZL-H-eN     "$PO" ZL $H $eN                      # + the closure's narrow accommodation
wf r17-cur-ZL-HO       "$PO" ZL $H $O
wf r18-cur-ZL-HO-eN    "$PO" ZL $H $O $eN
python3 $T/captures.py $W $T

# own -Dfortress.caches under <work-dir>.  Two checkers: the tracked one (with the count stage's

# is how perf-probes/nat/triage/run-all.sh took r17.  Variants (Library/ files copied, then edited):
#   base     the four files at the batch base d610695c0

#   seqgen   mine, with Condition.map returning SequentialGenerator[\G\] (the triage's ZL)

#   strtri   mine, with String's pair resolved the triage's way (the abstract pair deleted, the other kept)
set -u

S=com/sun/fortress; T=explorations/perf-probes/nat/triage; C=explorations/coordinator/tools/checker-count
CP=$(./bin/fortress_classpath 2>/dev/null | tail -1)
if [ ! -d "$W/tri-ponly-classes" ]; then
  rm -rf $W/ponly-src $W/tri-src; mkdir -p $W/ponly-src/$S $W/tri-src/$S
  for rel in scala_src/types/TypeAnalyzer.scala scala_src/types/TypeSchemaAnalyzer.scala scala_src/typechecker/TypeHierarchyChecker.scala; do
    mkdir -p $(dirname $W/ponly-src/$S/$rel); cp ProjectFortress/src/$S/$rel $W/ponly-src/$S/$rel; done
  mkdir -p $W/tri-src/$S/scala_src/typechecker; cp ProjectFortress/src/$S/scala_src/typechecker/OverloadingChecker.scala $W/tri-src/$S/scala_src/typechecker/
  patch -p8 -d $W/ponly-src/$S --forward < $T/p-only.patch || exit 1
  patch -p8 -d $W/tri-src/$S --forward < $T/overloading-checker.patch || exit 1
  mkdir -p $W/ponly-classes $W/tri-ponly-classes $W/stage-classes
  java -Xmx2g -cp "$CP" scala.tools.nsc.Main -d $W/ponly-classes -classpath "$CP" -encoding UTF-8 $(find $W/ponly-src -name '*.scala' | sort) || exit 1
  java -Xmx2g -cp "$CP" scala.tools.nsc.Main -d $W/tri-ponly-classes -classpath "$W/ponly-classes:$CP" -encoding UTF-8 $(find $W/tri-src -name '*.scala' | sort) || exit 1
  javac -nowarn -cp "$CP" -d $W/stage-classes $C/WorldFlip.java $C/shadow-src/$S/compiler/StaticChecker.java || exit 1
fi

import sys, io

s = io.open(p, encoding="utf-8").read(); assert s.count(a) == 1, (p, a, s.count(a))
io.open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(s.replace(a, b))
PY
}
for v in base mine rec broad seqgen zipnarrow strtri; do
  rm -rf $W/lib/$v; mkdir -p $W/lib/$v
  for f in $FILES; do
    if [ $v = base ]; then git show d610695c0:$f > $W/lib/$v/$(basename $f); else cp $f $W/lib/$v/; fi
  done
done
sub $W/lib/rec/FortressLibrary.fsi 'comprises { AnyIntegral, ... }' 'comprises { AnyIntegral }'
sed -i -E 's/([IJK]) extends AnyIntegral/\1 extends Integral[\\\1\\]/g' $W/lib/broad/RangeInternals.fsi
sub $W/lib/seqgen/FortressLibrary.fsi '    map[\G\](f: E->G): Condition[\G\]' '    map[\G\](f: E->G): SequentialGenerator[\G\]'
sub $W/lib/zipnarrow/List.fsi '  split(): (List[\E\], List[\E\])
  filter' '  split(): (List[\E\], List[\E\])
  zip[\F\](other: List[\F\]): ZeroIndexed[\(E,F)\]
  filter'
sub $W/lib/strtri/FortressLibrary.fsi '    abstract splitWithOffsets(): Generator[\(ZZ32, String)\]
    abstract split(): Generator[\String\]' '    splitWithOffsets(): Generator[\(ZZ32, String)\]
    split(): Generator[\String\]'
wf () { local out=$1 pre=$2 lib=$3; shift 3
  local c=$W/c-$out; rm -rf $c; mkdir -p $c
  timeout 900 java -Xmx4g -Xss64m "$@" -Dfortress.caches=$c -cp "$pre$W/stage-classes:$CP" WorldFlip $W/lib/$lib/FortressLibrary.fss > $W/$out.run.txt 2>&1
  printf '%-22s %s\n' "$out" "$(grep -oE 'has [0-9]+ errors?' $W/$out.run.txt | tail -1)"; }
PO="$W/tri-ponly-classes:$W/ponly-classes:"; HO="-Dprobe.triage.dropPHier=true -Dprobe.triage.dropPOver=true"
for v in base mine rec broad seqgen zipnarrow strtri; do wf $v-noP "" $v; done
for v in base mine rec seqgen; do wf $v-P "$PO" $v $HO; done
EOF

#!/bin/bash
# Compile-path ladder, restricted to the files this rung can affect.
#
# A copy of ../run-ladder.sh with two changes: the ladder root and output
# directory are private to this worktree, and the two whole-corpus loops are
# replaced by one driven by subset.txt (corpus<TAB>file per line).
#
# Pushes every interpreter test program (ProjectFortress/tests/*.fss) and every
# file in ProjectFortress/not_working_library_tests/ through the compiler path
# unchanged and records how far each one gets.
#
# Reproduce:  bash explorations/compile-ladder/run-ladder.sh
# Outputs:    explorations/compile-ladder/raw/<corpus>/<name>.{compile,run}
#             explorations/compile-ladder/results.tsv
#
# The run uses a private cache tree so it never touches default_repository/caches
# (fortress.caches system property + FORTRESS_CACHES env; ProjectProperties.java:283,
# same mechanism the suite uses at build.xml:941-943), and a private java.io.tmpdir
# so the 5.8 MB Rats! temp directory of every grammar-importing run (RatsUtil.java:138-144)
# is swept per file instead of filling the disk.

set -u

source "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../../../experiment/env.sh"

LADDER_ROOT="${LADDER_ROOT:-$FORTRESS_HOME/tmp/ladder-r1}"
export LADDER_CACHES="$LADDER_ROOT/ladder-caches"
export LADDER_TMP="$LADDER_ROOT/ladder-tmp"
export FORTRESS_CACHES="$LADDER_CACHES"
export JAVA_FLAGS="-Xmx2g -Xss64m -Dfortress.caches=$LADDER_CACHES -Djava.io.tmpdir=$LADDER_TMP"

PRISTINE="$LADDER_ROOT/pristine"
OUT="$FORTRESS_HOME/explorations/compile-ladder/repair-r1-atomic-static"
RAW="$OUT/raw"
TSV="$OUT/results.tsv"

COMPILE_TIMEOUT=120
RUN_TIMEOUT=60
MIN_FREE_KB=512000

mkdir -p "$RAW/tests" "$RAW/not_working_library_tests" "$LADDER_TMP"

disk_guard () {
    local free
    free=$(df -P / | awk 'NR==2{print $4}')
    if [ "$free" -lt "$MIN_FREE_KB" ]; then
        echo "STOP: only ${free} KB free on / (floor ${MIN_FREE_KB} KB)" | tee -a "$OUT/ladder.log"
        exit 2
    fi
    echo "-- disk free ${free} KB, cache $(du -sm "$LADDER_CACHES" | cut -f1) MB"
}

# Step 1: the compiler-world library, in the order repo-internals.md gives.
build_library () {
    cd "$FORTRESS_HOME/ProjectFortress" || exit 1
    local f
    for f in LibraryBuiltin/AnyType.fss LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fss \
             ../Library/CompilerLibrary.fss ../Library/CompilerAlgebra.fss \
             ../Library/CompilerSystem.fss ; do
        echo "library: $f"
        timeout 600 ../bin/fortress compile "$f" || { echo "LIBRARY BUILD FAILED on $f"; exit 1; }
    done
}

# Step 2: one known-good compiled program must print PASS before the ladder starts.
sanity () {
    cd "$FORTRESS_HOME/ProjectFortress" || exit 1
    timeout 200 ../bin/fortress compile library_tests/Integer1.fss > /dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
    timeout 60 ../bin/fortress run Integer1 2>&1 | grep -q PASS
}

# Keep only the library's own cache entries; a program's entries are never reused.
prune_cache () {
    ( cd "$LADDER_CACHES" && find . -type f -print ) | sort > "$LADDER_TMP/.now"
    ( cd "$PRISTINE" && find . -type f -print ) | sort > "$LADDER_TMP/.keep"
    comm -23 "$LADDER_TMP/.now" "$LADDER_TMP/.keep" | while read -r p; do
        rm -f "$LADDER_CACHES/$p"
    done
}

component_of () {
    # component/api name as declared, which is what `fortress run` wants
    sed -n 's/^[[:space:]]*\(component\|api\)[[:space:]]\+\([A-Za-z0-9_.]\+\).*/\2/p' "$1" | head -1
}

run_one () {
    local corpus="$1" path="$2"
    local base name comp crc rrc t0 t1 ct rt
    base=$(basename "$path")
    name="${base%.*}"
    comp=$(component_of "$path")
    [ -n "$comp" ] || comp="$name"

    t0=$(date +%s)
    timeout -k 5 "$COMPILE_TIMEOUT" ../bin/fortress compile "$path" \
        > "$RAW/$corpus/$base.compile" 2>&1
    crc=$?
    t1=$(date +%s); ct=$((t1-t0))

    rrc=""
    rt=""
    if [ "$crc" -eq 0 ] && [ "${base##*.}" = "fss" ]; then
        t0=$(date +%s)
        timeout -k 5 "$RUN_TIMEOUT" ../bin/fortress run "$comp" \
            > "$RAW/$corpus/$base.run" 2>&1
        rrc=$?
        t1=$(date +%s); rt=$((t1-t0))
    fi

    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' \
        "$corpus" "$base" "$comp" "$crc" "$rrc" "$ct" "$rt" >> "$TSV"
    echo "$corpus/$base crc=$crc rrc=$rrc ${ct}s"
}

main () {
    echo "=== ladder start $(date -Is) ==="
    disk_guard
    if [ ! -d "$PRISTINE" ]; then
        build_library
        rm -rf "$PRISTINE"; cp -a "$LADDER_CACHES" "$PRISTINE"
    fi
    sanity || { echo "SANITY FAILED: library_tests/Integer1 did not print PASS"; exit 1; }
    echo "sanity ok: library_tests/Integer1 compiles and prints PASS"
    prune_cache

    : > "$TSV"
    cd "$FORTRESS_HOME/ProjectFortress" || exit 1

    local n=0 line corpus f
    while IFS=$'\t' read -r corpus f; do
        [ -n "$corpus" ] || continue
        run_one "$corpus" "$corpus/$f"
        n=$((n+1))
        rm -rf "${LADDER_TMP:?}"/fortress*rats
        if [ $((n % 10)) -eq 0 ]; then prune_cache; disk_guard; fi
    done < "$OUT/subset.txt"
    prune_cache
    echo "=== ladder done $(date -Is), $n files ==="
    disk_guard
}

main "$@"

# Take the two microGPT programs through `fortress compile` in dependency order,
# in the same private cache as the ladder, and record the phase each component reaches.
set -u
source /home/user/fortress/experiment/env.sh
SP=/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-fortress/fe616d40-a9c6-56d7-9da1-7168a172765d/scratchpad
export LADDER_CACHES=$SP/measure/caches
export FORTRESS_CACHES=$LADDER_CACHES
export LADDER_TMP=$SP/measure/ladder-tmp
export JAVA_FLAGS="-Xmx2g -Xss64m -Dfortress.caches=$LADDER_CACHES -Djava.io.tmpdir=$LADDER_TMP"
RAW=/home/user/fortress/explorations/compile-ladder/baseline-2026-09-19/raw/microgpt
mkdir -p "$RAW"
TSV=$SP/measure/microgpt-results.tsv
: > "$TSV"
TIMEOUT=300

one () {  # dir file
  local dir="$1" f="$2" t0 t1 rc
  cd "/home/user/fortress/$dir" || exit 1
  t0=$(date +%s)
  timeout -k 5 $TIMEOUT ../../../bin/fortress compile "$f" > "$RAW/$f.compile" 2>&1
  rc=$?
  t1=$(date +%s)
  printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$dir" "$f" "$rc" "$((t1-t0))" >> "$TSV"
  echo "$dir/$f rc=$rc $((t1-t0))s"
  rm -rf "${LADDER_TMP:?}"/fortress*rats
}

done

done

# Rung L: the interpreter library's five plain api defects

problem: the count stage over the interpreter's library reads 93 before this rung, 26 of them `Ill-formed type` in `RangeInternals`, two duplicated `String` declarations and one covariant `zip`, explorations/compile-ladder/rung-library-defects/probes/checker-count-preedit.txt:15
spec: static-argument bounds, Specification/basic/trait-parameters.tex:43-50 with the calculus rule W-Tapp, Specification/appendices/calculi/basic/static.tex:229-246; overriding return types, Specification/basic/traits.tex:525-531; what an api's declarations oblige its component to contain, a `comprises { T, ... }` clause included, Specification/basic/components/source-code.tex:372-404
precedent: the api's own Integral-bounded factories (Library/RangeInternals.fsi:327); the explicit `abstract` pair added in commit d3bf13292; the component's own `Condition.map` (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:1226); the team's listed-plus-ellipsis api form, ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/Compiled10.pAPI.fsi:12
deviation: `QQ` reads `comprises { AnyIntegral, ... }`, not the record's `comprises { AnyIntegral }` (explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-3.md:97); `Condition.map` returns `Condition[\G\]` and the `String` pair keeps `abstract`, where the triage's copy wrote `SequentialGenerator[\G\]` and deleted the abstract pair; eleven declarations rebounded, not every `AnyIntegral` bound as that copy did, explorations/perf-probes/nat/zero/make-lib.py:65-92
historical: Library/RangeInternals.fsi:309, Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:373, Library/List.fsi:99

## In one paragraph

The rung repairs the five defects in the interpreter library's apis as the batch record describes them (`CLIMB-BATCH-3.md:93-97`), editing only `Library/RangeInternals.fsi`, `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi` and `Library/List.fsi`. Its test is the gate's count stage (`testIsStage`). The stage reads **93 before and 103 after** on this branch, where the record expected 102. The difference is one decision: `QQ`'s clause is `comprises { AnyIntegral, ... }` and not `comprises { AnyIntegral }`, because the component's `QQ` also comprises the private `Ratio` (`FortressLibrary.fss:524`, `:599`), and the specification requires an api clause that omits a component-private type to say `...` (`source-code.tex:386-392`). The one error that clause keeps is the checker's own defect: it refuses every api-declared trait that extends a `comprises { ..., ... }` trait, even one the clause lists (`TypeHierarchyChecker.scala:209-212`). That defect now has a gated expected-failure test (`compiler_tests/XXXComprisesEllipsisListed`), shown to go red under a deliberate local fix, and a provisional ledger row 354. Under rung P's measured placement, rebuilt here from the triage's committed patches, this library reads **24** where the record's text reads 23, and `Condition.map`'s unmasked error is gone. Thirteen interpreter programs print the same before and after, and the compiled-path ladder files that read these apis keep their phases and first errors.

## What I inherited, and one precondition that did not hold

The branch and the worktree did not exist when the rung started: no `/home/user/fortress-defects`, no local or remote `wip/rung-library-defects` (`git ls-remote origin 'refs/heads/wip/*'` listed only earlier batches' branches), and none of the other five worktrees either. The workflow launches "after the worktrees exist" (`explorations/coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.js:16-17`). I created mine alone, by the recipe at `explorations/coordinator/remote-container.md:96-110`: `git worktree add -b wip/rung-library-defects /home/user/fortress-defects d610695c0c014001687e528fa9fd99078db6ea76`, a copy of `ProjectFortress/build`, `mkdir tmp`, and `git push -u origin wip/rung-library-defects`. That wrote worktree metadata into the main tree's `.git`; nothing in the main tree's working files was read for the work or changed. So nothing was inherited and nothing needed re-verifying. `ant compileAll` in the fresh worktree took 1 min 34 s. It also deleted the tracked `default_repository/caches/global.map`, which the later `fortress compile` runs recreated; I restored it with `git checkout` and it is in none of this branch's commits.

## The test: the count stage, before and after

`explorations/coordinator/tools/checker-count/run.sh`, run in this worktree after `ant compileAll` and before any edit, then again after the edit:

| api | before | after |

After the red demonstration below was reverted and rebuilt, a last stage run produced a table byte-identical to the post-edit capture.

The rows overlap and count an error more than once (`CLIMB-BATCH-3.md:67`), so what moved is read from the distinct errors. `probes/errset.py` lists them from each full output; `LC_ALL=C comm` of the two lists:

## Where these fixes belong

These are api-level errors. The interpreter never reports them: it checks no static-parameter bound, and it stores a `comprises` clause without validating it (`interpreter/evaluator/BuildEnvironments.java:887-891`). The checker reports them only because the stage runs the compiler's static checker over the interpreter's library. For each defect the candidates were the api, the component, or the checker. By the specification passages below, the api is wrong in defects 1 to 4, and the checker is right to refuse it. In defect 5 the api was wrong, and the checker is wrong about the corrected api. ## The five, one by one

### 1. Family C: eleven `RangeInternals.fsi` declarations bounded by `Integral[\I\]`

**Measurement.** 26 errors at 15 sites. Each is `Ill-formed type: X[\I\]. The static argument I does not satisfy the corresponding bound Integral[\I\]`. It is raised where a declaration whose own `I` is unbounded or bounded by the non-parametric `AnyIntegral` names one of the four traits declared `[\I extends Integral[\I\]\]` (`RangeInternals.fsi:44`, `:121`, `:235`, `:304`).

**Specification.** A type parameter's `extends` clause is its bound (`trait-parameters.tex:43-50`). An instantiation `C[\T\]` is well-formed only when each argument is a subtype of its parameter's bound with the arguments substituted: rule W-Tapp, `appendices/calculi/basic/static.tex:229-246` (`\dsyntaxWB`, `\wBothRule` at `latex-common/macros/calculus-macros.tex:423`, `:531`). The prose chapter defines the bound and the calculus states the check; the prose has no sentence of its own for it. I grepped `Specification/basic/` for `bound`, `satisf`, `well-formed` and `static argument`, and none of the hits states the check.

**Precedent.** The api's own factories for the same types already carry the bound: `rightScalarRange[\I extends Integral[\I\]\]` (`:327`), `fullScalarRange` (`:570`), `open` (`:172`).

**Edit.** `object RightScalarRange[\I\]` (`:309`) and `emptyScalarRange[\I\]()` (`:578`) gain the bound; `sized1Range`/`sized2Range`/`sized3Range` (`:580-585`), `bounded1Range`/`bounded2Range`/`bounded3Range` (`:587-592`) and the three `openRangeHelper` (`:612-616`) change `X extends AnyIntegral` to `X extends Integral[\X\]`. That is 11 declarations and 20 bounds; the brief's "fifteen" counts the sites. The bound only, as the brief requires.

**Decision: the narrow set, not every `AnyIntegral` bound.** The triage's copy replaced every `AnyIntegral` bound in the file (`explorations/perf-probes/nat/zero/make-lib.py:65-80`), which also covers `left1Range` … `open3Range` (`:594-622`). Those twelve are well-formed in the api, because `LeftRange[\I\]` and its siblings are unbounded, so the checker says nothing about them. Measured (below, `broad-noP`): the broad set also reads 103. I kept the narrow one because the rule is the smallest edit the test needs.

**What it leaves, not measured.** The component declares the same eleven with the same bounds (`RangeInternals.fss:681`, `:1418`, `:1422-1437`, `:1482-1486`). The export check compares static-parameter bounds for equality (`scala_src/typechecker/ExportChecker.scala:604`, `:619-627`), and the specification's satisfaction rule for functions compares parameter and return types only (`source-code.tex:355-360`). So once `RangeInternals.fss` is checked, the implementation's export check will report the api and component bounds as different. The component's bodies also carry the family-C defect itself. And the public range factories pass an `AnyIntegral`-bounded `I` into these helpers (`FortressLibrary.fsi:2161-2215`, `FortressLibrary.fss:3816-3860`), so the bound will have to travel up to them. None of this can be measured today: no component is reached while its api has errors. It is the next library batch's.

### 2. Family D: `trait String`'s two declarations of `split` and `splitWithOffsets`

**Measurement.** Two errors, "multiple declarations … with the same parameter type: ()", at `FortressLibrary.fsi:2311`/`:2327` and `:2312`/`:2328`.

**What the component defines.** The component's `trait String` (`FortressLibrary.fss:3958-4103`) declares **neither** method. The bodies are in the objects that extend it: `String.fss:156-157`, `:317-318`, `:445`, and `FlatString.fss:146-147`.

**Specification.** A trait declaration in an api is satisfied by a component declaration that contains "for each field declaration and non-abstract method declaration in the exported declaration, a satisfying declaration" (`source-code.tex:372-384`). So a non-abstract api declaration that the component's trait does not declare is unsatisfied, and the pair that survives must be `abstract`.

**History.** The documented pair is the older one: it began as `subdivide()` in commit `855a4699d` (2008-08-27) and was renamed before November. Andrew Black added the explicit `abstract` pair in `d3bf13292` (2008-11-14) and left the old pair in place. The component had no body for either at that commit.

**Edit.** The `abstract` pair and the blank lines added with it (`:2311-2314`) are deleted. The documented pair (`:2327-2328`, now `:2323-2324`) gains `abstract`, so the doc comment stays with the declarations it documents.

**Decision: the abstract form, against the triage's copy.** That copy deleted the abstract pair and kept the plain one (`make-lib.py:82-85`). ### 3. Family F: `List.fsi:99`'s `zip`

**Measurement.** One error: the return type `Generator[\(E,F)\]` is not a subtype of the inherited `ZeroIndexed[\(E,F)\]` (`FortressLibrary.fsi:1187`).

**Specification.** Two dotted methods where one's parameter is a strict subtype of the other's are a valid overloading only if the return types agree the same way (the Subtype Rule for dotted methods, `advanced/overloading.tex:168-173`). `List[\F\]` is a strict subtype of `ZeroIndexed[\F\]` through `LexicographicOrder` (`FortressLibrary.fsi:1199-1200`).

### 5. The `comprises` clause at `FortressLibrary.fsi:373`, and a decision against the record's text

**Measurement.** `Invalid comprises clause: a trait with a comprises ..., such as FortressLibrary.QQ, should not be extended.`, reported at `:409`, where `AnyIntegral`, declared in the same api, extends `QQ`.

**The record's fix, and why I did not take it.** The record writes `comprises { ... }` → `comprises { AnyIntegral }` (`CLIMB-BATCH-3.md:97`), measured 93 → 92. The component's clause is `comprises { Ratio, AnyIntegral }` (`FortressLibrary.fss:524`), and `Ratio` is declared only in the component (`:599`, absent from the api). The specification allows an api's clause to omit a component-private type only through `...`: "If a trait declaration (in an API) has a comprises clause containing '…', then the comprises clause of its satisfying declaration must contain all the types listed in the declaration in the API but it cannot contain '…'; instead, it may contain other types declared in the component provided that those types are not declared by the API" (`source-code.tex:386-392`). Without `...`, the component's header must be the same up to order (`:372-378`). The grammar provides the form for exactly this case, `TraitType (, TraitType)* [, ...]` (`components/apis.tex:52-60`), and the parser accepts it (`parser/NoNewlineHeader.rats:116-123`). The traits note says the same (`traits.tex:231-241`): the types listed are exactly the immediate subtraits and must extend `T`, and the others "may not be declared or imported by the API".

So `comprises { AnyIntegral }` makes the api state that `QQ`'s only immediate subtrait is `AnyIntegral`, which is false for `Ratio`. The implementation agrees with the specification here, and the probes show it both ways:

- `probes/ComprisesClosed.fss`/`.fsi` is the record's shape in miniature: api `trait T comprises { O }`, component `trait T comprises { O, P }` with a private `object P`. For the library that is `Ratio` at `FortressLibrary.fss:599`, invisible today only because the component is not reached. The export check would add `different comprises clauses for traits` (`ExportChecker.scala:363-365`, `:720-735`, which accepts `{ AnyIntegral, ... }` against `{ Ratio, AnyIntegral }`).
- `comprises { AnyIntegral, ... }` is exactly the team's own `Compiled3.q` (`test_library/Compiled3.q.fsi:13-14`, component `compiler_tests/Compiled3.q.fss`: api `T comprises { O, ... }` with `O` declared in the api, component adds a private `P`). The checker refuses it with the same message this rung keeps (`probes/compiled3q-compile.txt`).

**Edit.** `trait QQ … comprises { AnyIntegral, ... }`.

**What the kept error is.** `TypeHierarchyChecker.scala:209-212` refuses any api-declared trait extending a trait whose clause has `...`, whether the clause lists it or not. The same checker requires every listed type to extend the trait (`:231-236`). Together the two rules make the grammar's listed-plus-ellipsis form unusable, which the specification's text rules out. This is a checker defect, and the specification settles it. Its home is below.

**What this costs the batch.** The record's clause reads 102 on this branch and 23 merged; this one reads 103 and 24. The only difference, with or without P, is that one `:409` error (`probes/differentials.txt`, "distinct-error differences"). With the checker's refusal repaired, this library reads 102, the record's number (`probes/checker-count-with-deliberate-checker-fix.txt`). If Pavol prefers the record's text, the edit is one token and the three probes above say what it costs.

## Where these fixes belong

These are api-level errors. The interpreter never reports them: it checks no static-parameter bound, and it stores a `comprises` clause without validating it (`interpreter/evaluator/BuildEnvironments.java:887-891`). The checker reports them only because the stage runs the compiler's static checker over the interpreter's library. For each defect the candidates were the api, the component, or the checker. By the specification passages below, the api is wrong in defects 1 to 4, and the checker is right to refuse it. In defect 5 the api was wrong, and the checker is wrong about the corrected api. The components are not edited: `RangeInternals.fss` is what the interpreter runs, the stage cannot reach any component while its api has errors, and the brief confines L to the three `.fsi` files.

## The five, one by one

### 1. Family C: eleven `RangeInternals.fsi` declarations bounded by `Integral[\I\]`

**Measurement.** 26 errors at 15 sites. Each is `Ill-formed type: X[\I\]. The static argument I does not satisfy the corresponding bound Integral[\I\]`. It is raised where a declaration whose own `I` is unbounded or bounded by the non-parametric `AnyIntegral` names one of the four traits declared `[\I extends Integral[\I\]\]` (`RangeInternals.fsi:44`, `:121`, `:235`, `:304`).

**Specification.** A type parameter's `extends` clause is its bound (`trait-parameters.tex:43-50`). An instantiation `C[\T\]` is well-formed only when each argument is a subtype of its parameter's bound with the arguments substituted: rule W-Tapp, `appendices/calculi/basic/static.tex:229-246` (`\dsyntaxWB`, `\wBothRule` at `latex-common/macros/calculus-macros.tex:423`, `:531`). The prose chapter defines the bound and the calculus states the check; the prose has no sentence of its own for it. I grepped `Specification/basic/` for `bound`, `satisf`, `well-formed` and `static argument`, and none of the hits states the check.

**Precedent.** The api's own factories for the same types already carry the bound: `rightScalarRange[\I extends Integral[\I\]\]` (`:327`), `fullScalarRange` (`:570`), `open` (`:172`).

**Edit.** `object RightScalarRange[\I\]` (`:309`) and `emptyScalarRange[\I\]()` (`:578`) gain the bound; `sized1Range`/`sized2Range`/`sized3Range` (`:580-585`), `bounded1Range`/`bounded2Range`/`bounded3Range` (`:587-592`) and the three `openRangeHelper` (`:612-616`) change `X extends AnyIntegral` to `X extends Integral[\X\]`. That is 11 declarations and 20 bounds; the brief's "fifteen" counts the sites. The bound only, as the brief requires.

**Decision: the narrow set, not every `AnyIntegral` bound.** The triage's copy replaced every `AnyIntegral` bound in the file (`explorations/perf-probes/nat/zero/make-lib.py:65-80`), which also covers `left1Range` … `open3Range` (`:594-622`). Those twelve are well-formed in the api, because `LeftRange[\I\]` and its siblings are unbounded, so the checker says nothing about them. Measured (below, `broad-noP`): the broad set also reads 103. I kept the narrow one because the rule is the smallest edit the test needs.

**What it leaves, not measured.** The component declares the same eleven with the same bounds (`RangeInternals.fss:681`, `:1418`, `:1422-1437`, `:1482-1486`). The export check compares static-parameter bounds for equality (`scala_src/typechecker/ExportChecker.scala:604`, `:619-627`), and the specification's satisfaction rule for functions compares parameter and return types only (`source-code.tex:355-360`). So once `RangeInternals.fss` is checked, the implementation's export check will report the api and component bounds as different. The component's bodies also carry the family-C defect itself. And the public range factories pass an `AnyIntegral`-bounded `I` into these helpers (`FortressLibrary.fsi:2161-2215`, `FortressLibrary.fss:3816-3860`), so the bound will have to travel up to them. None of this can be measured today: no component is reached while its api has errors. It is the next library batch's.

### 2. Family D: `trait String`'s two declarations of `split` and `splitWithOffsets`

**Measurement.** Two errors, "multiple declarations … with the same parameter type: ()", at `FortressLibrary.fsi:2311`/`:2327` and `:2312`/`:2328`.

**What the component defines.** The component's `trait String` (`FortressLibrary.fss:3958-4103`) declares **neither** method. The bodies are in the objects that extend it: `String.fss:156-157`, `:317-318`, `:445`, and `FlatString.fss:146-147`.

**Specification.** A trait declaration in an api is satisfied by a component declaration that contains "for each field declaration and non-abstract method declaration in the exported declaration, a satisfying declaration" (`source-code.tex:372-384`). So a non-abstract api declaration that the component's trait does not declare is unsatisfied, and the pair that survives must be `abstract`.

**History.** The documented pair is the older one: it began as `subdivide()` in commit `855a4699d` (2008-08-27) and was renamed before November. Andrew Black added the explicit `abstract` pair in `d3bf13292` (2008-11-14) and left the old pair in place. The component had no body for either at that commit.

**Edit.** The `abstract` pair and the blank lines added with it (`:2311-2314`) are deleted. The documented pair (`:2327-2328`, now `:2323-2324`) gains `abstract`, so the doc comment stays with the declarations it documents.

**Decision: the abstract form, against the triage's copy.** That copy deleted the abstract pair and kept the plain one (`make-lib.py:82-85`). Both give 103 (`strtri-noP` below), and `String` and `FlatString` fall to 0 either way; adding `abstract` raised no abstract-method error in the api objects `FlatString`, `CatString`, `EmptyString` and `SubString` (`FlatString.fsi:16`, `String.fsi:16-22`). The specification decides it.

### 3. Family F: `List.fsi:99`'s `zip`

**Measurement.** One error: the return type `Generator[\(E,F)\]` is not a subtype of the inherited `ZeroIndexed[\(E,F)\]` (`FortressLibrary.fsi:1187`).

**Specification.** Two dotted methods where one's parameter is a strict subtype of the other's are a valid overloading only if the return types agree the same way (the Subtype Rule for dotted methods, `advanced/overloading.tex:168-173`). `List[\F\]` is a strict subtype of `ZeroIndexed[\F\]` through `LexicographicOrder` (`FortressLibrary.fsi:1199-1200`).

**The absent body.** `Library/List.fss` has no `zip` at all. Every `li.zip(lj)` already runs the inherited `ZeroIndexed.zip`, whose body is `FortressLibrary.fss:1721-1722` (`DefaultZip`). It accepts a `List[\F\]` and returns `ZeroIndexed[\(E,F)\]`.

**Edit and decision: drop the declaration, rather than narrow its return type.** Narrowing keeps an api method that the component's trait `List` contains nothing to satisfy (`source-code.tex:381`, `:399-404`), and it promises nothing the inherited method does not already promise. Dropping makes the api say what the component provides. Both clear the error (`zipnarrow-noP` also reads 103). The three interpreter programs that call `zip` print the same (below).

**Same defect elsewhere.** `PureList.fsi:75` has the identical declaration and `PureList.fss` has no body for it either: one more site. It is not measured, because the `PureList` api stops at an earlier error (defect list, row 355).

### 4. Family F, unmasked by P: `Condition.map`

**Measurement.** Invisible on this branch (absent from the 93) and present once rung P's relaxation is on. I measured it here instead of leaving it to the gather. `differentials.sh` rebuilds P's measured placement from the triage's committed patches (`explorations/perf-probes/nat/triage/p-only.patch`, `overloading-checker.patch`, switches `dropPHier` and `dropPOver`) into this worktree's `tmp/`, exactly as `triage/run-all.sh` does. Under it the base library reports `For map, the return type of [\G\](Condition[\()\], ()->G)->Generator[\G\] @ FortressLibrary.fsi:789 should be a subtype of … SequentialGenerator[\G\] @ :762` (`base-P`), and this rung's library does not (`mine-P`: zero `For map` errors).

**Specification.** The return type of an overriding declaration must be a subtype of the overridden one's (`traits.tex:525-531`). An equal parameter type replaces the inherited declaration (`traits.tex:461-466`).

**Edit and decision.** `map[\G\](f: E->G): Condition[\G\]` (`:789`). The triage's copy used `SequentialGenerator[\G\]` (`make-lib.py:87-88`). I chose `Condition[\G\]` for three reasons. It is what the component declares (`FortressLibrary.fss:1226`), and the export check compares return types for equality (`ExportChecker.scala:598-610`). It is the more precise promise: a mapped `Condition` is again a `Condition`. And every api override of it already returns a subtype of `Condition[\G\]`: `Just` (`:848`), `Nothing` (`:872`), `NotUnique` (`:914`). By count the two are the same (`seqgen-noP` 103, `seqgen-P` 24). `ivmap` (`:790`) has the same api/component difference (`Generator[\G\]` against `Condition[\G\]`, `.fss:1228`). No checker error names it, so it is not touched.

### 5. The `comprises` clause at `FortressLibrary.fsi:373`, and a decision against the record's text

**Measurement.** `Invalid comprises clause: a trait with a comprises ..., such as FortressLibrary.QQ, should not be extended.`, reported at `:409`, where `AnyIntegral`, declared in the same api, extends `QQ`.

**The record's fix, and why I did not take it.** The record writes `comprises { ... }` → `comprises { AnyIntegral }` (`CLIMB-BATCH-3.md:97`), measured 93 → 92. The component's clause is `comprises { Ratio, AnyIntegral }` (`FortressLibrary.fss:524`), and `Ratio` is declared only in the component (`:599`, absent from the api). The specification allows an api's clause to omit a component-private type only through `...`: "If a trait declaration (in an API) has a comprises clause containing '…', then the comprises clause of its satisfying declaration must contain all the types listed in the declaration in the API but it cannot contain '…'; instead, it may contain other types declared in the component provided that those types are not declared by the API" (`source-code.tex:386-392`). Without `...`, the component's header must be the same up to order (`:372-378`). The grammar provides the form for exactly this case, `TraitType (, TraitType)* [, ...]` (`components/apis.tex:52-60`), and the parser accepts it (`parser/NoNewlineHeader.rats:116-123`). The traits note says the same (`traits.tex:231-241`): the types listed are exactly the immediate subtraits and must extend `T`, and the others "may not be declared or imported by the API".

So `comprises { AnyIntegral }` makes the api state that `QQ`'s only immediate subtrait is `AnyIntegral`, which is false for `Ratio`. The implementation agrees with the specification here, and the probes show it both ways:

- `probes/ComprisesClosed.fss`/`.fsi` is the record's shape in miniature: api `trait T comprises { O }`, component `trait T comprises { O, P }` with a private `object P`. It is refused *in the component*: `ComprisesClosed.T has a comprises clause but its immediate subtype P is not eligible to extend it` (`probes/comprises-closed-compile.txt`). For the library that is `Ratio` at `FortressLibrary.fss:599`, invisible today only because the component is not reached. The export check would add `different comprises clauses for traits` (`ExportChecker.scala:363-365`, `:720-735`, which accepts `{ AnyIntegral, ... }` against `{ Ratio, AnyIntegral }`).
- `comprises { AnyIntegral, ... }` is exactly the team's own `Compiled3.q` (`test_library/Compiled3.q.fsi:13-14`, component `compiler_tests/Compiled3.q.fss`: api `T comprises { O, ... }` with `O` declared in the api, component adds a private `P`). The checker refuses it with the same message this rung keeps (`probes/compiled3q-compile.txt`).

**Edit.** `trait QQ … comprises { AnyIntegral, ... }`.

**What the kept error is.** `TypeHierarchyChecker.scala:209-212` refuses any api-declared trait extending a trait whose clause has `...`, whether the clause lists it or not. The same checker requires every listed type to extend the trait (`:231-236`). Together the two rules make the grammar's listed-plus-ellipsis form unusable, which the specification's text rules out. This is a checker defect, and the specification settles it. Its home is below.

**What this costs the batch.** The record's clause reads 102 on this branch and 23 merged; this one reads 103 and 24. The only difference, with or without P, is that one `:409` error (`probes/differentials.txt`, "distinct-error differences"). With the checker's refusal repaired, this library reads 102, the record's number (`probes/checker-count-with-deliberate-checker-fix.txt`). If Pavol prefers the record's text, the edit is one token and the three probes above say what it costs.

## The differentials

`probes/differentials.sh`, output `probes/differentials.txt`. The four api files are copied into library directories and each copy is edited. The same driver and instrumented checker as the stage are used, each run under a private cache. `mine-noP`'s distinct-error list is identical to the in-tree stage run's, which validates the copy mechanism, and `base-noP` reproduces 93.

| variant | what differs from this rung's library | tracked checker | with P's placement |
|---|---|---|---|
| base | the batch base's four files | 93 | 33 (the triage's r13) |
| mine | nothing | **103** | **24** (`FortressLibrary` 6, `RangeInternals` 42) |
| rec | `QQ comprises { AnyIntegral }` | 102 (r27) | 23 (r17) |
| broad | every `AnyIntegral` bound in `RangeInternals.fsi` replaced | 103 | — |
| seqgen | `Condition.map` returns `SequentialGenerator[\G\]` | 103 | 24 |
| zipnarrow | `List.zip` kept, narrowed to `ZeroIndexed[\(E,F)\]` | 103 | — |
| strtri | `String`: abstract pair deleted, plain pair kept | 103 | — |

The crash line is `NativeArray … Not yet implemented` in every run. The P column is the triage's placement rebuilt from its patches, not rung P's branch, which this rung cannot see. The merged tree's number is the gather's to confirm.

## What proves nothing broke

**Interpreter programs, before and after** (`run-controls.sh`; captures `probes/controls-pre/` and `probes/controls-post/`, each file ending in `EXIT=`). These are the six the brief names: `ArrayListQuick`, `PureListQuick`, `CovariantTest` (they call `zip`), `StringTests` (`splitWithOffsets`), `Generator2Test` and `ArrayScalarExtension`. I added seven: `RationalTest` (`QQ`/`Ratio`), `RangeTest`, `rangeOperators`, `OpenRangeCase` (the range factories), `maybeTest`, `conditionalGenerator` (`Condition`) and `LongStringTests`. Each ran from a cold cache on both sides, with `default_repository/caches` emptied before the post-edit run. All 13 exit 0 before and after. The outputs are byte-identical except the two `Succeeded in 0.6xxs` timing lines of `ArrayListQuick` and `PureListQuick`. This matters because the interpreter does derive exclusion from `comprises` (`interpreter/evaluator/types/FType.java:280-296`). Evidently it reads the component's declarations, not the api's. `ant testSystem` is the gate's.

**The compiled path's ladder** (step 7). I add no names, so by the rule the subset is empty. But the record's reason for no ladder move ("L and C edit `Library/`, which is the interpreter's prelude and not the compiled path's") is imprecise: compiled programs that `import List` or `FortressLibrary` do read these files. So I ran, before (the three files at the batch base) and after, the nine `tests/` programs whose recorded compiles cite `List.fsi` and the eighteen microGPT components. The driver is `run-subset.sh`, the repair batch's with `OUT` taken from `LADDER_OUT` and the eighteen compiled-only as `microgpt-phase.sh` does; the subset is `subset.txt`, under a private ladder root. Results: `ladder-before/` and `ladder-after/`, classified by the baseline's `classify.py`; every raw difference is in `probes/ladder-before-after-diff.txt`.

- The two `ladder.tsv` files are identical except the seconds column.
- The two `microgpt.tsv` files are identical: phase `disambiguate` and the same first error for all eighteen.
- The raw outputs differ only in `List.fsi:110`/`:113` → `:109`/`:112`, and in three microGPT components whose error counts fall by 2 (`AplMgSyntax.fsi`/`.fss` 1380 → 1378, `MicroGptApl.fss` 1492 → 1490). In the compiled world, `Generator` in the deleted `String` pair was an ambiguous name, and `Condition.map` swaps one ambiguous `Generator` for one ambiguous `Condition`.

None of the 85 pass-list files imports an edited api (checked by grep), and the gate compares the eighteen by phase only.

## Every measured defect and its home

1. **Home 1, repaired here, asserted by the gated stage.** Family C (26 errors), family D (2), `List.zip` (1): the stage's `#total` of 103 and its `String`, `FlatString`, `List` and `RangeInternals` rows, declared as `expectedCheckerCount: 103`. For `Condition.map` the batch's declared exception applies (`CLIMB-BATCH-3.md` "How it is run", rule 2): its assertion is the merged tree's stage, and this rung has shown the error gone under P's placement.
2. **Home 2, deferred with the specification settling it: the checker's refusal of a listed type in `comprises { T, ... }`.** `TypeHierarchyChecker.scala:209-212` against `source-code.tex:386-392`, `apis.tex:52-60`, `traits.tex:231-241`. The gated expected-failure test is `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/XXXComprisesEllipsisListed.test` with `ComprisesEllipsisListed.fss`/`.fsi` beside it: `QQ`'s shape, a listed api trait and a component-private object. It asserts that the program compiles, which the specification says it must.
   - Today: `probes/junit-xxx-expected.txt` ("Saw expected failure", the refusal at `.fsi:3`).
   - With a deliberate local fix at `:209` (`probes/deliberate-checker-fix.txt`: skip the refusal when `comprisesContains(subst_comprises, tt, …)`), rebuilt: `probes/junit-xxx-goes-red.txt` ("Missing expected failure … Expected failure or exception, saw none", `Tests run: 1, Failures: 1`).
   - Reverted and rebuilt: `probes/junit-xxx-green-again.txt`.
   - The same deliberate fix makes the stage read 102 and lets `Compiled3.q` compile (`probes/compiled3q-compile-with-fix.txt`). It also lets `Compiled10.p` compile (`probes/compiled10p-compile-with-fix.txt`), which the specification refuses: its `U` extends `T comprises { S, ... }` from a component that does not export `T`'s api (`traits.tex:236-241`). Today that program is refused only through the over-broad rule, at the wrong place (`S` in the api, `probes/compiled10p-compile.txt`). So the real repair has two parts, and the ledger row says so.
   - The team's `XXX3q.test` and `XXX10p.test` record the over-broad refusal as their expected output and pass today only because their expected text does not match. After any fix they would stay expected failures, so neither would signal it. That is why the new test is needed.
3. **The fourth case, the specification settling a defect whose repair is outside this rung: `PureList.fsi`.** Measured by pointing the stage's driver at `Library/PureList.fsi` (`probes/purelist-api-run.txt`). `trait List[\E\] extends { Equality[\E\], ZeroIndexed[\E\] }` (`PureList.fsi:41`) is `Ill-formed type: Equality[\E\]`: `E` does not satisfy `Equality`'s bound (`FortressLibrary.fsi:73`). The sibling `List.fsi:67` reads `LexicographicOrder[\List[\E\],E\]`, so the defect is the declared type, not a bound. That is a type change, out of this rung's scope, and the batch's stop in any case. It masks `PureList.fsi:75`, the `zip` this rung dropped from `List.fsi`. No gated test can reach `PureList` (it is not in the stage's import closure, and nothing compiles against the interpreter's library), so the home is a ledger row with the probe, provisional row 355.

Measured but not new homes: the 39 new `RangeInternals` errors belong to the stage's declared total and the triage's classification (`perf-probes/nat/triage/classified-203.txt`), and the record assigns 19 of them to P's overloading half. Derived but not measured: the component-side bounds and the public range factories (defect 1, "What it leaves").

## Grep for competing declarations (step 6)

The one new name is the test component `ComprisesEllipsisListed`, with api-local `Q`, `A`, `R`. It is absent from `ProjectFortress/tests`, every `ProjectFortress/*_tests`, `test_library`, `Library` and `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress` (grep, no hits). The edits add no library name.

## For the gather

- **Line shifts.** `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi` loses four lines after `:2310`: `:2526` → `:2522` (the record's `RelationalPredicateCondition` citation), `:2327-2328` → `:2323-2324`, and rung C's scalar block `:2540-2547` → `:2536-2543`. `:373`, `:409`, `:789` and C's `Array3` clause at `:1655-1659` do not move. `Library/List.fsi` loses one line after `:98`. `Library/RangeInternals.fsi` does not shift.
- **Rule 1.** C edits `FortressLibrary.fsi` at the closure (`:409`); this rung edits `:373` and touches no declaration C touches.
- **Manifest.** L: `expectedCheckerCount: 103`, and no `expectedCheckerCrash`. The merged expectation with P becomes **24**, with a `FortressLibrary` row of 6 (3 distinct: `:2522`, the closure reported at `:411`, and `QQ`'s at `:409`), `RangeInternals` 42 and the crash unchanged. The compiler-test track gains one test, `XXXComprisesEllipsisListed`, which reports "Saw expected failure".

## Not done

- No `ant testFast`/`ant testSystem` (the gate's).
- The component-side bounds and the range factories (defect 1) are derived, not measured.
- The second part of the checker repair (row 354): refusing a non-listed extension outside the exporting component. No test pins that `Compiled10.p` must stay refused.
- `ivmap`'s api/component return-type difference.
